title: The Last Bell
premise: Xanthe Sandoval is sent to appraise Hollowmere House, a colonial-era estate whose paperwork never quite matches its rooms. As they document the property, the mirrors begin reflecting one second late—and the lag grows, showing Xanthe things they did before they did them. They learn the town's founders built the house as an instrument: a ledger that collects the memories of everyone who signs its papers, feeding on the forgetting that survival requires. The last resident, dying matriarch Odile Ferrar, has kept the ritual unfinished for decades to trap the house's hunger inside herself. Xanthe must complete the founders' ritual—signing themselves into the ledger and giving up their own worst memory—before Odile signs the final papers and the house is freed to take the whole town. In the end, Xanthe finishes the ritual, losing the memory of the accident that made them a survivor, and walks out of Hollowmere documented by the house instead of documenting it.
about_author: Silas Thornbury spent eleven years as a county archivist before turning to fiction, a career that left him with a professional reverence for records and a private distrust of what they omit. He writes in a converted surveyor's office in upstate New York, where he claims the filing cabinets are load-bearing in more ways than one.

chapters.title: The Square Footage of Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe Sandoval arrives at Hollowmere House to appraise it for the Ferrar estate, armed with laser measures and a habit of narrating their findings aloud. The rooms don't sum correctly—the total is always one room larger than the parts. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into the first real fear.

chapters.title: Odile, Holding Still
chapters.summary: Xanthe meets the last resident, Odile Ferrar, ninety-one and sharp as a deed restriction, who insists on being present for every measurement. She asks strange questions: what Xanthe has survived, what they refuse to remember. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: wary fascination; Odile is either a threat or a warning.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: While photographing the upstairs hallway, Xanthe notices their own reflection in a mirror moves a beat late. They test it scientifically—metronome, stopwatch, video—and the lag is real, and growing. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the comfort of method collapsing against evidence.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Xanthe finds Hollowmere's original deed, signed by eleven founders, with a codicil written in a hand that isn't any of theirs. The codicil describes the house as 'a vessel for what is set down.' POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: discovery as dread—the paperwork is the haunting.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: The mirrors begin showing the room as it was decades ago: a séance, a signing, eleven founders feeding pages into the walls. Xanthe realizes the house replays memory, not light. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past is not past here, it is stored.

chapters.title: The Room That Isn't Measured
chapters.summary: Xanthe finally finds the extra room: a windowless study behind the pantry, lined floor to ceiling with ledgers, each one a former resident's life in the founders' handwriting. Odile's ledger is the thickest. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: horror of being read—the house has been reading Xanthe since arrival.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile admits she was supposed to complete the ritual at twenty-five and refused; her refusal trapped the house's hunger in her body, which is why she has not died. Every year she doesn't sign, the house takes a memory from the town instead. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: guilt worn smooth by decades of endurance.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets
chapters.summary: Xanthe canvasses Hollowmere village and finds a community with suspicious gaps: no one remembers 1974, or their own weddings, or why the war memorial has no names. The house has been eating. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the price of survival made civic and visible.

chapters.title: The Lag Reaches Ten
chapters.summary: The mirror delay hits ten seconds, and Xanthe watches their reflection do something they haven't done yet: sign a page. They photograph it and the photo shows the page already signed. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: free will fraying—the house is drafting them.

chapters.title: The Ritual, Half-Read
chapters.summary: Deciphering the founders' codicil, Xanthe learns the ritual requires three acts: witness, record, and relinquish—the signer must give the ledger their worst memory as payment. The founders all flinched at the third act. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the trap's mechanism revealed—power corrupts even the pious.

chapters.title: Xanthe's Own Ledger
chapters.summary: In the hidden study, Xanthe finds a ledger already begun in their name, documenting their life with terrible accuracy—except for one redacted page where their handwriting dissolves. They cannot read what they most need to give up. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: confrontation with the wound the whole book has circled.

chapters.title: The Accident
chapters.summary: A fragment surfaces: Xanthe survived a crash that killed their sister, and has built a life on not remembering the ten seconds before impact—the same duration as the mirror lag. The house has been counting down their forgetting. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: grief breaking through the armor of documentation.

chapters.title: Heirs and Assigns
chapters.summary: A Ferrar cousin arrives to expedite the sale, eager for Odile to sign and die so the estate clears. The house warms to him visibly—doors opening, mirrors clearing—and Xanthe understands it is courting a new vessel. POV: cousin Marcus. Emotional beat: banal greed as the horror's perfect host.

chapters.title: Odile Fails
chapters.summary: Odile attempts the ritual one last time and cannot relinquish her memory of the man she let die in 1974; the house punishes the town with a night of mass amnesia. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the tragedy of a protector whose strength is exactly what damns her.

chapters.title: The Founders' Mistake
chapters.summary: Xanthe realizes the founders never intended a vessel—they intended to become the house's masters, and it ate them instead. Power over the ledger was always the ledger's power over them. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: thematic crystallization—no one signs this contract and stays whole.

chapters.title: Marcus Signs
chapters.summary: Marcus forges Odile's signature to close the sale early; the papers accept it, and the house begins detaching from its moorings—mirrors showing whole streets, walls sweating ink. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: triumph turning to consumption as the ledger starts writing him.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of Marcus
chapters.summary: Xanthe finds Marcus in the hidden study, half-dissolved into his own ledger, still smiling, still rich on paper. Odile, dying, tells Xanthe the ritual can still be completed by anyone willing to pay the third price. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: pity and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: First act of the ritual: Xanthe walks the house and consciously witnesses everything it has taken—the town's stolen weddings, funerals, and 1974—speaking each memory aloud so the house must hold them as seen. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: documentation as prayer, made literal and costly.

chapters.title: Record
chapters.summary: Second act: Xanthe writes their own account of Hollowmere into the founders' ledger, in their surveyor's hand, claiming the house in the only way it fears—by describing it exactly. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: fierce, exhausted clarity; the pen as weapon.

chapters.title: Relinquish
chapters.summary: Third act at the threshold of the hidden study: to pay the price, Xanthe must surrender the ten seconds before the crash—the memory that made them a survivor. They sign, and the redacted page fills with their sister's face. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the book's heart; survival's price finally paid in full.

chapters.title: The Last Bell
chapters.summary: The house rings a bell that no one installed, and every mirror in Hollowmere shows the present tense again. Odile dies at peace; the ledgers go blank; Marcus is a man who remembers being rich and nothing else. POV: Odile, in her final hour. Emotional beat: release after long captivity.

chapters.title: Appraised
chapters.summary: Xanthe files their report on Hollowmere House—accurate to the square foot, the extra room included—and cannot remember why their eyes sting at the sister's name in an old phone. The final mirror shows them a full second early, as if the house is saying thank you. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: survival achieved, and the quiet grief of not knowing what it cost.
